I think about this year the same way I did last year, and the year before. My land is not much — six mu and a half. Two big children work outside, so it is mostly me and my man in the field, and the old people help a little.

I keep one and a half mu for cotton, near the house where I can watch it every day. Cotton needs the eye — you must see it. The rest, five mu, I do wheat in winter then corn in summer, same as everyone around me. That is how this land eats and pays.

For wheat I buy one bag of compound fertilizer for each mu before planting — the blue bag, 40 jin each, the man at the shop says it is 15-15-15. Then when the wheat stands up in spring I spread urea, about 30 jin one mu. Some years I add a little more if the leaves look yellow. I water the wheat four times — once before winter so it does not die from cold, then at green-up, jointing, and when the grain is filling. Without water the wheat is nothing here. I spray maybe two times, for the bugs and the rust.

For corn after wheat, the time is tight. I buy another bag of compound per mu and throw urea when it is knee-high, about 40 jin each mu — corn eats heavy. I water one time, maybe two if the sky is dry. Spray one time for the borer, sometimes two.

Cotton takes the most work and the most spray. I use one bag compound per mu at planting, and urea when it flowers, maybe 30 jin. Cotton bugs never stop — I spray five or six times through summer, my back hurts from the pump. I water three times. The seed I buy is the kind my neighbor Li planted last year, she got good bolls.

I do not change much. Changing costs money and if the harvest is bad, five people still need to eat. Better to spend a little extra on fertilizer than see the wheat thin. The ground plough I hire from the tractor man — 50 yuan one mu, he does it in one morning.
